key_insight: For semilinear parabolic PDEs, neural approximation costs separate into governing-law structure and data encoding, with polynomial nonlinearities admitting logarithmic-size constitutive blocks.
engineering_relevance: The results motivate PDE-aware architectures whose nonlinear blocks and learned weights per encoded mode need not grow with grid refinement or smaller time steps.
method: Characterize constitutive-law complexity using an exponent determined by its computation graph.
Separate nonlinear-law approximation from data encoding with bounded learned weights per mode.
Establish whole-trajectory approximation bounds and near-matching lower bounds for viscous Hamilton–Jacobi equations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical guarantees, including O(log(1/η)) nonlinear-block size for 2D Navier–Stokes and roughly η^(-1/s) parameters for viscous Hamilton–Jacobi equations with C^s Hamiltonians, with matching lower bounds up to logarithms.
watch_item: These are approximation guarantees, not demonstrated training or runtime guarantees; total data-encoding cost still depends on the number of encoded modes.
paper_title: Neural Network Approximation and Structural Complexity of Semilinear PDEs with Lower Bounds
